For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension one with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, the standing Cohen–Macaulay curve hypotheses imply $X$ is connected, Cohen–Macaulay and purely one-dimensional. Let $\omega_X$ be its coherent dualizing module, equal to $H^{-1}(f^!k)$ for the structure map $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Its genus is $g=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. A regular global section of an invertible sheaf is one whose multiplication map $\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal L$ is injective; an ample invertible sheaf is very ample if its global sections define a closed immersion into projective space.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension at most $1$ and an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal L$, put $\deg_k(\mathcal L)=\chi(X,\mathcal L)-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$, where $\chi(X,\mathcal F)=\dim_kH^0(X,\mathcal F)-\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal F)$. A linear series $\mathfrak g_d^r$ is a pair $(\mathcal L,V)$ with $\deg(\mathcal L)=d$ and $V\subseteq H^0(X,\mathcal L)$ a $(r+1)$-dimensional $k$-subspace. On a nonsingular curve the image of $V\otimes_k\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal L$ is invertible, giving a morphism $\varphi_{(\mathcal L,V)}:X\to\mathbf P_k^r$ and an injection $\varphi^*\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^r}(1)\hookrightarrow\mathcal L$ carrying standard coordinate sections to a chosen basis of $V$.

Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a proper scheme over $k$ having dimension $1$
and $H^0(X, \mathcal{O}_X) = k$. Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible
$\mathcal{O}_X$-module. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{L}$ has a regular global section,
\item $H^1(X, \mathcal{L}) = 0$, and
\item $\mathcal{L}$ is ample.
\end{enumerate}
Then $\mathcal{L}^{\otimes 6}$ is very ample on $X$ over $k$.
